Actual Article Body:

The ACT Director of Public Prosecutions is appealing a sentence in which a 16-year-old boy who raped a woman at a house party avoid jail.

Login or signup to continue reading

In an ACT Supreme Court decision published last month, the rapist was handed an 18-month prison sentence, suspended upon him entering into a good behaviour order. This means his sentence was to be served in the community, rather than behind bars.

The grounds on which the prosecuting office is appealing the sentence are not known at this stage.

The teenage boy had moved to Australia from Bhutan about six months before the attack, and admitted the rape was his first sexual experience.

Justice Andrew Muller found his "limited insight into societal norms in Australia" reduced his moral culpability.

The judge took into account his young age and said his prospects for rehabilitation were "significantly improved" if he was allowed to remain in the community with close supervision.

The teenager, who cannot be named due to his age, previously pleaded guilty to a rolled-up count of sexual intercourse without consent.

The sentence sparked debate with advocates for sexual assault victims calling for an ACT government review of sentencing laws and practices.

An online petition calling for Justice Muller to be stood down from his position also received almost 7000 signatures.

In 2025, the then 16-year-old met the 18-year-old victim for the first time at a house party. She agreed to go for a walk and they consensually kissed.

They sat down in a nearby green belt before he ripped open her clothing and sexually assaulted her multiple ways.

The victim later said she "just froze" and felt "trapped under him". She didn't want anything sexual to happen but didn't know how to say so.

She described the acts as "rough and really unpleasant" and said she wanted to run away but was scared the boy would hurt her.

In a victim impact statement, she described feeling a loss of dignity, confidence and sense of self.

She said she "can no longer call [her] body [her] own" and that night her life was stolen and would forever be changed.
